title: docs: document merge queue state machine
description:
The merge queue has 9 status values but ARCHITECTURE.md only lists 4.

Full state machine to document:
- none → pending → acquiring → merging → merged/failed
- merging → resolving → resolved (conflict path)
- merged → merged_needs_repair (validation failure path)
- skipped (no changes)

Add to docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:
- Complete list of all merge statuses
- State transition diagram (ASCII or mermaid)
- When each status is set
- How validation/repair affects final status

title: Create pkg/daemon/websocket.go with WebSocket Hub (clients map, broadcast/register/unregister channels) and Client struct. Implement Run() goroutine pattern for connection management and broadcasting.
Detect and handle 'work already done' gracefully
description:
## Problem

When multiple agents work on similar tasks, or a task is retried after partial success, the second agent may complete with no changes because the work was already done. Currently this:
1. May spawn a resolver unnecessarily
2. Shows as 'failed' or confusing status
3. No clear indication that 'work already done' is a valid outcome

## Proposed Solution

1. **Detection**: Check if agent's intended changes match current state
2. **Status**: Add 'skipped' or 'already_done' status distinct from 'failed'
3. **Tracking**: Record why no changes were needed (already applied, duplicate task, etc.)
4. **UI**: Show this state clearly in dashboard (green checkmark, not red X)

## Use Cases
- Retry after daemon restart picks up task that was already merged
- Two agents assigned similar/overlapping tasks
- Agent completes but resolver finds nothing to do

## Related
- canopy-7n96: Added 'skipped' merge status for resolver with no changes
- canopy-xurd: Don't spawn resolver when agent has no git changes

title: Persist task_description to SQLite
description:
## Problem

## Current Flow

- Sent via IPC and available in event payload
- Displayed in AgentDetail.tsx (lines 188-195)
- **NOT** extracted in `handleAgentStarted` (persistence_handler.go)
- **NOT** in `persistence.Agent` struct
- **NOT** in SQLite agents table

## Solution
1. Add migration V12: `ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN task_description TEXT`
2. Add `TaskDescription` field to `persistence.Agent` struct
3. Update `agentColumns` and `agentColumnsWithPrefix`
4. Update CreateAgent/UpdateAgent queries to include task_description
5. Update scanAgent/scanAgentFromRows to read task_description
6. Update `handleAgentStarted` to extract and save task_description

## Files to Modify
- pkg/persistence/migrate.go (add V12)
- pkg/persistence/store.go (Agent struct, queries, scan functions)
- pkg/daemon/persistence_handler.go (extract task_description in handleAgentStarted)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] task_description persisted to SQLite on agent start
- [ ] task_description loaded from database on state restoration
- [ ] Detail pane shows task_description after daemon restart

title: Persist repair agent state through daemon restart
description:
## Summary

Ensure repair agent state persists through daemon restarts.

## New Fields

### persistence.Agent
```go

    // ... existing fields ...
    RepairAttempts    int       `json:"repair_attempts"`
    LastRepairOutput  string    `json:"last_repair_output"`
    ValidationStatus  string    `json:"validation_status"`  // pending, passed, failed, repairing
}
```

### Database Migration
```sql
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN repair_attempts INTEGER DEFAULT 0;
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN last_repair_output TEXT;
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN validation_status TEXT DEFAULT 'pending';
```

## State Restoration

On daemon restart:
1. Load agents with validation_status = 'repairing'
2. Resume repair from last attempt number
3. Continue retry loop

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New fields added to persistence.Agent
- [ ] Database migration for new columns
- [ ] ConvertPersistenceAgentToState maps new fields
- [ ] Repair state restored on daemon restart
- [ ] In-flight repairs resume correctly

title: Dashboard crashes when clicking Rules (funnel) button - undefined.length error
description:
## Problem
Clicking the funnel/filter (Rules) button on the right side of the dashboard causes the entire UI to disappear with a JavaScript error:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'length')
    at m_ (index-BF7esirj.js:485:4467)
```

The UI briefly flashes before disappearing and doesn't recover on refresh (due to localStorage persisting the expanded state).

## Root Cause
In `web/dashboard/src/components/rules/ConfigSettingsCard.tsx`, lines 104, 109, 114 access `.length` on `config.types`, `config.exclude_types`, and `config.exclude_labels` without null checks:

```tsx
{config.types.length > 0 && (
{config.exclude_types.length > 0 && (
{config.exclude_labels.length > 0 && (
```

The Go backend returns `null` for empty slices (Go nil slices serialize to JSON null), but the TypeScript interface `ConfigRulesSettings` declares these as `string[]` assuming they're always arrays.

## Fix
Add null coalescing to handle undefined arrays:
```tsx
{(config.types?.length ?? 0) > 0 && (
{(config.exclude_types?.length ?? 0) > 0 && (
{(config.exclude_labels?.length ?? 0) > 0 && (
```

Also fix `handleStartEdit` (lines 34-36) which spreads these potentially undefined arrays:
```tsx
types: [...(config.types ?? [])],
exclude_types: [...(config.exclude_types ?? [])],
exclude_labels: [...(config.exclude_labels ?? [])],
```

## Files to modify
- `web/dashboard/src/components/rules/ConfigSettingsCard.tsx`

title: Token/cost display missing for some completed agents
description:
## Problem

Some completed worker task cards show token count and cost, but others show nothing or zeros.

## Root Cause

Token data is only populated when `EventAgentCompleted` event is processed:

1. **Real-time flow**: `handleAgentCompleted()` in state.go extracts token fields from event payload
2. **Persistence flow**: persistence_handler.go saves tokens to database on completion
3. **Restoration flow**: `ConvertPersistenceAgentToState()` reads from database

## Conditions Causing Missing Data

1. Agent completed but `EventAgentCompleted` event never arrived (IPC issue, daemon crash)
2. Agent completed during daemon downtime - never persisted
3. Older agents from before token tracking have NULL database fields
4. Agent failed early before token metrics were generated
5. Database row created but completion update never applied

## Solution Options

1. **Ensure completion events always fire**: Add retry/persistence for completion events
2. **Backfill from Claude API**: If agent has session ID, query actual usage
3. **Show placeholder**: Display "--" instead of hiding when data unavailable
4. **Persist partial data**: Save token data incrementally during agent execution, not just at completion

## Related

Token data flow:
- `pkg/daemon/state.go:1065-1079` - event handler
- `pkg/daemon/persistence_handler.go:228-239` - persistence
- `web/dashboard/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx:225-233` - display

title: Repository abstraction: Add explicit Repository entity for multi-repo dashboard support
description:
## Problem

Repositories are implicit throughout the canopy stack - just WorkDir strings passed around, never modeled as first-class entities. This causes:

1. Dashboard beads pane can only show one repo (the CWD where daemon started)
2. Persistence (runs.db) has no repo_id - can't filter history by repository  
3. New daemon starts with empty dashboard despite having run history in database
4. IPC events don't include repository context

## Solution

Introduce an explicit Repository entity that provides stable identity:

- Repository registry in $XDG_CACHE_HOME/canopy/repositories.json
- Add repo_id FK to runs/agents tables in runs.db
- Update IPC protocol to include repo context
- Dashboard repo selector dropdown
- Proper state restoration on daemon startup

## Key Design Decisions

1. Repository identity stored centrally (not in repo itself) - keeps repos portable
2. Dashboard shows one repo at a time via dropdown selector
3. Beads remain scoped to individual repos (no cross-repo dependencies)
4. Migration support for existing runs.db data

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Repository selector dropdown in dashboard header
- [ ] Switching repos updates beads pane and filters history
- [ ] Daemon startup restores state from database correctly
- [ ] Existing databases migrate seamlessly

title: Preserve agent patches when merge and resolution both fail
description:
## Problem

When an agent's merge fails and the subsequent resolver agent also fails, the agent's work (git patches) is permanently lost. This is a data loss bug.

## Root Cause

In `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go`:

1. Original agent completes successfully with patches in `result.GitState.Patches`
2. `MergeSingle()` fails to apply patches (conflict)
3. Resolver is spawned with patches written to `.canopy/conflict/patch-*.patch` in its overlay
4. Resolver fails
5. **Original agent's overlay is cleaned up at line 443**: `o.cleanupOverlay(result)`
6. Resolver overlay is left dangling in temp dir (no cleanup on failure path, line 418-424)
7. **On orchestrator.Cleanup() (line 717), entire tempDir is removed**: `os.RemoveAll(o.tempDir)`

Result: All patches are lost.

## Code References

- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:418-424` - resolver failure path (no patch preservation)
- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:443` - original overlay cleanup
- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:717` - tempDir removal

## Solution

When both merge and resolution fail, preserve patches to a persistent location:

Option A: Save to repo under `.canopy/failed-patches/<task-id>/`
Option B: Save to cache dir under `~/.cache/canopy/failed-patches/<task-id>/`
Option C: Store in runs.db as blob for later retrieval

Recommend Option B to keep repos clean while maintaining persistence.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] When merge fails and resolver fails, patches are preserved
- [ ] Preserved patches are accessible after orchestrator cleanup
- [ ] Clear error message tells user where to find preserved patches
- [ ] Patches can be manually applied later via `git am`

title: Orchestrator does not send initial task list to daemon for persistence
description:
## Problem

When `canopy run` starts orchestration, it loads tasks from beads but does not send them to the daemon as `EventTaskUpdated` events. The only place tasks get persisted to SQLite is:

1. `loadTasksFromBeads()` - which requires a beads client factory (see canopy-zrvg)
2. `EventTaskUpdated` events during merge queue status changes (mergequeue/processor.go:442)

The `canopy run` command reads tasks via `beadsClient.Ready(ctx)` at run.go:293 but only sends `SendRunStarted()` with a count, not individual task details.

## Impact

- SQLite tasks table only gets populated during merge operations
- On daemon restart, tasks visible during previous runs are missing
- Dashboard state doesn't match actual beads state

## Solution Options

1. **Orchestrator sends initial tasks**: After loading ready tasks, send `SendTaskUpdated()` for each task
2. **Rely on canopy-zrvg fix**: If daemon can load from beads JSONL, this may be less critical
3. **Both**: Send events AND have daemon load from beads for redundancy

title: Process groups: ensure agent processes die with orchestrator
description:
## Problem

Agents spawned via `exec.CommandContext()` are independent processes, not children of the orchestrator. If the orchestrator dies unexpectedly:
- Agent processes continue running as orphans
- Resources consumed without supervision
- Daemon marks them as failed on restart, but processes keep running until natural completion

## Solution

Use Unix process groups so killing the orchestrator kills its agents:

```go
// In pkg/agent/executor.go, when spawning agent
cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
    Setpgid: true,  // Create new process group with agent as leader
}

// Store pgid for cleanup
// On orchestrator shutdown/context cancellation:
syscall.Kill(-pgid, syscall.SIGTERM)
```

## Implementation Notes

1. **executor.go**: Add `Setpgid: true` to SysProcAttr when creating command
2. **executor.go**: Track process group ID after Start()
3. **scheduler.go** or **orchestrator.go**: On shutdown, kill process groups for any running agents
4. **Consider graceful shutdown**: SIGTERM first, SIGKILL after timeout

## Documentation Updates

Update AGENTS.md or create an ARCHITECTURE.md to document these explicit IPC architectural decisions:

### Process Hierarchy
- Agents are child processes of their orchestrator via process groups
- Orchestrator death triggers agent termination (no orphans)
- Daemon only interacts with orchestrators, never agents directly

### Agent-Orchestrator Communication  
- One-way: stdout/stderr streaming from agent to orchestrator
- No bidirectional IPC by design - agents are black-box CLI executions
- Cancellation via signals (SIGTERM/SIGKILL), not messages

### Agent-Daemon Isolation
- Agents have zero knowledge of daemon (no socket path, no URLs)
- All status flows: Agent → stdout → Orchestrator → IPC → Daemon
- Security boundary: agents may run sandboxed (bubblewrap), untrusted

### Daemon Restart Resilience
- Orchestrators queue IPC events during daemon downtime (10k capacity)
- Reconnection with exponential backoff (100ms → 5s, 5 min timeout)
- No message loss - queue flushes on reconnection

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Agents terminate when orchestrator is killed (SIGTERM or SIGKILL)
- [ ] No orphan agent processes after orchestrator crash
- [ ] Graceful shutdown: SIGTERM to agents, wait, then SIGKILL if needed
- [ ] Architecture documentation added/updated with IPC design decisions
- [ ] Existing tests pass
- [ ] Manual verification: kill orchestrator mid-run, confirm agents die

title: Merge queue leaks .canopy/conflict/ files into commits
description:
## Problem

The merge queue doesn't filter out `.canopy/` directory files during merge. When a resolver agent runs, it writes to `.canopy/conflict/` in its overlay. These files then get merged into the working directory and staged/committed.

## Root Cause

In `pkg/merge/sequential.go`:
- `isBeadsFile()` filters `.beads/` (line 178-181)
- No equivalent filter for `.canopy/`
- Resolver writes to `.canopy/conflict/` (see `pkg/resolver/resolver.go:222`)
- These files get applied via `applyChange()` and staged

## Evidence

Commit cdb2e59 incorrectly included:
```
.canopy/conflict/errors.txt
.canopy/conflict/original-task.txt
.canopy/conflict/patch-0.patch
```

## Solution

Add `isCanopyFile()` check and filter `.canopy/` in the merge loop:

```go
func isCanopyFile(path string) bool {
    return path == ".canopy" || strings.HasPrefix(path, ".canopy/")
}
```

Apply in the same places as `isBeadsFile()` (lines 107, 159).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.canopy/` files are never merged from overlays
- [ ] `.canopy/` files are never staged or committed
- [ ] Resolver conflict context still works (files are in overlay only)

title: Refactor canopy run CLI to delegate to daemon
description:
## Summary

Transform `canopy run` from an orchestration owner to a thin client that delegates to the daemon.

## Current State

- `canopy run` creates orchestrator directly
- Orchestrator runs in CLI process
- CLI process must stay alive for run to continue
- IPC sends events one-way to daemon

## Target State

- `canopy run` tells daemon to start a run
- Daemon owns orchestrator (see sibling task)
- CLI streams output from daemon
- CLI can disconnect without stopping run (daemon continues)

## Implementation

1. New daemon API endpoint:
   ```
   POST /api/runs/start
   {
     "repo_path": "/path/to/repo",
     "concurrency": 4,
     "sandbox": true,
     "max_retries": 3,
     "priority_max": 2,
     "types": ["bug", "task"],
     "exclude_labels": ["wip"],
     "indefinite": false
   }
   ```
   
   Response:
   ```
   {
     "run_id": "run-abc123",
     "status": "started"
   }
   ```

2. Refactor `cmd/canopy/run.go`:
   - Parse flags into RunConfig struct
   - POST to daemon `/api/runs/start`
   - Subscribe to WebSocket for run events
   - Print events to stdout (same format as before)
   - Handle Ctrl+C: detach or stop (configurable)

3. CLI flags (strict filters only):
   - `--priority N`: Sets `priority_max = N`
   - `--type bug,task`: Filter by type
   - `--label X`: Include label
   - `--exclude-label X`: Exclude label
   - `--detach`: Start run and exit immediately
   - `--attach <run-id>`: Attach to existing run
   - `--stop`: Stop active run for current repo
   - `--status`: Show active run status

4. Deprecated flags (warn and ignore):
   - `--prompt`: Use explicit filters instead
   - `--stop-at-gate`: Use `--exclude-label checkpoint` instead

5. WebSocket subscription:
   - Filter events by run_id
   - Format and print to terminal
   - Handle reconnection gracefully

## Backward Compatibility

- Same CLI interface for basic usage
- Same output format
- Deprecated flags print warning but don't break

## Dependencies

- Move orchestrator lifecycle into daemon
- Singleton enforcement (for --stop to work correctly)

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐

│ ○ Worker Agent        ✓ Complete   2m 15s      │
```

title: Merge/validation/repair status not persisted - Details drawer empty after restart
description:
## Problem

After daemon restart, the Details drawer on worker agent cards is missing because all the data needed to determine `hasWorkerChainData` is either not persisted or lost.

## hasWorkerChainData Check

```typescript
const hasWorkerChainData = Boolean(
  agent.merge_status ||         // ❌ Empty - not persisted
  agent.validation_status ||    // ❌ Empty - not persisted
  agent.repair_attempts ||      // ❌ Always 0 - not persisted
  childAgents.length > 0        // ✓ Works IF child agents exist
);
```

## What's Broken

### 1. Merge/Validation/Repair Status (P0)
- `merge_status`, `validation_status`, `repair_attempts` are all empty in SQLite
- The persistence handler code exists (`handleAgentMergeStatus`) but events aren't reaching it
- **NO test coverage** for `EventAgentMergeStatus` persistence flow
- This affects ALL agents, including those without child agents

### 2. Child Agent Linkage (Works, but not sufficient alone)
- Resolver/repair agents ARE persisted with `parent_agent_id`
- `RebuildAgentChildLinks()` rebuilds `ChildAgentIDs` on restore
- Child agents are correctly grouped in dashboard
- BUT: Agents without conflicts/repairs have no children, so they rely entirely on merge_status

## Impact

- **Agents with child agents**: Details button MAY show (via childAgents.length > 0)
- **Agents without child agents**: Details button NEVER shows after restart (all other fields are empty)

## Evidence

```sql
SELECT merge_status, validation_status, repair_attempts FROM agents LIMIT 5;
-- All empty/0

SELECT COUNT(*) as total, COUNT(CASE WHEN parent_agent_id <> '' THEN 1 END) as children FROM agents;
-- 399 total, 75 children (81% have no children and thus no Details after restart)
```

## Root Cause

`EventAgentMergeStatus` events are either:
1. Not being sent by merge processor (IPC client issue?)
2. Not being received by daemon (connection issue?)
3. Not being handled correctly (payload format issue?)

The persistence handler code exists but has zero test coverage, so the bug went undetected.

## Fix Required

1. Add test coverage for `EventAgentMergeStatus` → `handleAgentMergeStatus` flow
2. Debug why merge events aren't being persisted (trace IPC flow)
3. Verify agent IDs match between run.go callbacks and merge processor
4. Ensure validation/repair status updates also persist correctly

## Files Involved

- pkg/daemon/persistence_handler.go:104 (handler exists but broken/untested)
- pkg/daemon/persistence_handler_test.go (NO merge status tests!)
- pkg/mergequeue/processor.go:680 (sends merge status)
- pkg/ipc/server.go:368 (converts to event)
- web/dashboard/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx:140 (hasWorkerChainData)

title: Merged badge inconsistent due to camelCase vs snake_case field mismatch
description:
## Problem

Some worker task cards show "Merged" badge while others don't, even when they should.

## Root Cause

The AgentCard component checks **two different field names**:

```typescript
// web/dashboard/src/components/agents/AgentCard.tsx:244-270
{(agent.mergeStatus || agent.merge_status) && (
  {(agent.mergeStatus === 'merged' || agent.merge_status === 'merged') ? (
```

- **Real-time agents**: Use `merge_status` (snake_case from IPC protocol)
- **Historical agents**: Use `mergeStatus` (camelCase from persistence layer)

## Conditions Causing Missing Badge

1. Agents restored from database have `mergeStatus` but component may prioritize wrong field
2. Real-time agents get `merge_status` from IPC events
3. Field name mismatch between Go JSON tags and TypeScript interfaces
4. Persistence handler only persists final merge statuses (`merged`/`failed`), not intermediate

## Solution

Standardize on one field name throughout the stack:
- Go struct JSON tags should use `merge_status` (snake_case per API conventions in AGENTS.md)
- TypeScript interfaces should use `merge_status`
- Remove duplicate field checks in AgentCard

beads.Client not thread-safe despite concurrent access
description:
## Problem

The beads.Client wraps CLI calls to bd without any synchronization, but is accessed concurrently by:
- Orchestrator (reading ready tasks)
- Scheduler callbacks (marking tasks in_progress/done)
- MergeCoordinator (marking tasks done/failed after merge)

Location: pkg/beads/client.go

## Race Condition Example

1. Agent A completes, calls beadsClient.Done(taskA)
2. Agent B completes simultaneously, calls beadsClient.Done(taskB)
3. Both spawn bd close processes that open the beads DB
4. SQLite BUSY error or data corruption

The comment in pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:95 mentions 'beadsMu' but it's never actually used to protect the client!

## Impact

- Can corrupt the beads database
- Causes tasks to be marked incorrectly
- Hard to reproduce race conditions in production

## Suggested Fix

Add a mutex to serialize beads operations:

```go
type Client struct {
    bdPath  string
    workDir string
    mu      sync.Mutex  // Serialize all bd operations
}

func (c *Client) run(args ...string) (string, error) {
    c.mu.Lock()
    defer c.mu.Unlock()
    // ... existing implementation
}
```

title: Update resolver prompt with three-way merge context
description:
## Task

Rewrite the resolver prompt to properly explain the three-way merge situation and provide clear guidance on how to handle concurrent changes.

### Current Issues with Prompt

The current prompt says:
- "HEAD has moved" (vague)
- "Apply the SAME changes from the patches" (doesn't address concurrent changes)
- Doesn't explain that concurrent changes should be preserved

### New Prompt Content

```markdown
## Three-Way Merge Resolution

**You are resolving a git merge conflict using three-way merge semantics.**

### The Three Versions

1. **BASE** (`.canopy/conflict/base/`): The codebase when the original agent started.
   The patches in `patch-*.patch` are diffs relative to this state.
   Commit: {BaseCommit}

2. **OURS** (current HEAD): The codebase now, after other agents merged their work.
   This is what you see in the working directory.

3. **THEIRS** (`.canopy/conflict/patch-*.patch`): The changes the original agent made.
   These are expressed as diffs from BASE.

### What Happened

While the original agent worked on BASE, other changes were merged:
```
{ConcurrentDiff summary - first N lines or file list}
```

These concurrent changes are VALID and MUST be preserved.

### Your Goal

Produce code that has BOTH:
1. All the concurrent changes that are already in HEAD (OURS)
2. The intent of the patches (THEIRS), adapted for the new context

**DO NOT revert any code that exists in HEAD but not in the patches.**
The patches were created against BASE, not HEAD. Missing lines in patches
don't mean those lines should be removed - they mean those lines were
added concurrently and must stay.

### Resolution Process

1. Read the patches to understand what the agent INTENDED to change
2. Read `.canopy/conflict/base/` to see original file states
3. Look at the current files (OURS) to see concurrent changes
4. Apply the INTENT of the patches to the current state
5. Preserve all concurrent changes from OURS
```

### Testing

- Resolver correctly preserves concurrent changes
- Resolver correctly applies intended changes
- Prompt is clear about the three-way semantics

title: Resolver changes never merged: agent.Result.Overlay is never set
description:
## Problem

Resolver agent changes are never merged to the repository because the `agent.Result.Overlay` field is never populated, causing the merge condition to always fail.

## Root Cause

1. `agent.Result` has an `Overlay *sandbox.Overlay` field (executor.go:34)
2. The executor never sets this field - overlay is passed as a parameter but never assigned to `result.Overlay`
3. In both merge paths, the check fails:
   - processor.go:165: `if resolverResult.AgentResult.Overlay != nil`
   - orchestrator.go:453: `if resolverResult.AgentResult.Overlay != nil`
4. Since `Overlay` is always nil, `MergeSingle` is NEVER called for resolver results
5. Resolver's changes exist only in memory/overlay and are never committed

## Impact

- Resolver runs successfully and makes changes
- Changes are never merged to the actual repository
- Task is marked as done anyway (false success)
- User sees "Conflict resolved successfully" but no commits are created
- This explains the user report: "patches applied to HEAD but NOT committed"

## Solution

Set `result.Overlay = overlay` in executor.Execute() before returning, OR change the resolver's handling to pass the overlay explicitly rather than relying on the Result field.

## Code References

- `pkg/agent/executor.go:34` - Overlay field defined but never set
- `pkg/mergequeue/processor.go:165` - Check that always fails
- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go:453` - Same failing check

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Executor sets result.Overlay = overlay before returning
- [ ] Resolver merge path successfully calls MergeSingle
- [ ] Resolver changes are committed to the repository
- [ ] Add test to verify resolver merging works end-to-end
close_reason: Fixed by setting result.Overlay = overlay in executor.Execute()

title: Merge queue pause race condition: new beads picked up before pause takes effect
description:
## Problem

When a merge resolver is spawned, the merge queue doesn't appear to pause immediately. This could be due to:

1. **Race condition**: A new bead is picked up for work in the window between deciding to spawn a resolver and the pause actually taking effect
2. **Pause not working**: The pause mechanism itself may have a bug

## Observed Behavior

Merge resolver spawns but the queue continues processing, potentially picking up new work that should wait for the merge conflict to be resolved.

## Investigation Areas

1. Check the timing between `SpawnMergeResolver()` and `Pause()` calls
2. Verify the pause flag is being checked atomically in the work-pickup loop
3. Look for any goroutine scheduling issues where work selection happens before pause is visible
4. Check if there's a buffered channel or pending work that continues after pause

## Expected Behavior

When a merge resolver is spawned, no new beads should be picked up until the merge is resolved and the queue is resumed.

## Files to Investigate

- `pkg/mergequeue/processor.go` - Merge queue processing logic
- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` - Agent spawning and coordination

title: Add periodic beads sync to daemon
description:
## Summary

Now that the daemon controls everything, beads for a repository should periodically sync on their own. Currently sync is purely on-demand:
- Manual: `canopy sync-beads`
- Startup: `loadTasksFromBeads()` on daemon init
- Repo switch: `loadTasksFromBeads()` when active repo changes

## Current Architecture

The daemon has all the infrastructure needed:
- **EventBus**: Pub/sub for broadcasting `EventStateSync` after updates
- **RepositoryManager**: Manages active repo, caches beads clients per repo
- **BeadsClient**: Mutex-serialized CLI wrapper that calls `bd` commands
- **Persistence**: SQLite stores tasks, WebSocket hub broadcasts to dashboard

## Proposed Design

Add a `PeriodicSyncManager` component:

```
PeriodicSyncManager:
├── Config: interval (default 30s), enabled flag, mode (active/all repos)
├── Background goroutine started in daemon.Start()
├── time.NewTicker(interval) for scheduling
├── Per tick:
│   ├── Get repos to sync (active or all registered)
│   ├── Call existing sync logic (loadTasksFromBeads)
│   ├── Broadcast EventStateSync
│   └── Handle errors gracefully (log, continue)
├── Graceful shutdown: Stop ticker on daemon.Stop()
└── Optional: file watcher integration for immediate sync on .beads changes
```

## Key Files

- `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` - add manager field, integrate into lifecycle
- `pkg/daemon/periodic_sync.go` (new) - manager implementation
- `pkg/daemon/beads_handlers.go` - refactor common sync logic if needed
- `pkg/daemon/lifecycle_manager.go` - coordinate startup order

## Design Considerations

1. **Concurrency**: BeadsClient already uses mutex; RuntimeState uses sync.RWMutex
2. **Error handling**: Non-fatal; log errors, continue on next tick
3. **Performance**: Consider debouncing if adding file watcher
4. **Config**: Interval and enabled flag should be configurable (possibly per-repo)

title: Sandbox hardening: Complete and validate isolation mechanisms
description:
## Problem

Canopy's sandbox has known security gaps documented in SANDBOX-DESIGN.md:

1. **Network access unrestricted** - Agents can exfiltrate data, SSRF, crypto mining
2. **Disk quotas not enforced** - Agents could fill disk
3. **Seccomp filtering missing** - Dangerous syscalls not blocked
4. **macOS lacks namespace isolation** - Only APFS clones, no capability dropping
5. **No comprehensive test suite** - Security claims not validated

## Solution

Complete the Phase 1-3 roadmap from SANDBOX-DESIGN.md and add thorough testing.

## Key Design Decisions

1. Network isolation via slirp4netns proxy
2. Disk quotas via XFS/btrfs or overlay size limits
3. Seccomp via libseccomp with allowlist approach
4. macOS: Document limitations clearly, explore sandbox-exec
5. Integration tests that verify isolation properties

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Network access controllable (allow/deny/proxy)
- [ ] Disk usage bounded per agent
- [ ] Dangerous syscalls blocked on Linux
- [ ] Security test suite passes
- [ ] Documentation accurate for all platforms

title: Implement repair retry limit and exhaustion handling
description:
## Summary

Implement retry logic for repair agents with bead filing on exhaustion.

## Configuration

In validation.toml:
```toml
[validation]
max_repair_attempts = 3  # Default: 3
```

## Behavior

1. Validation fails → spawn repair agent (attempt 1)
2. Re-run validation
3. If still fails → spawn repair agent (attempt 2) with history
4. Re-run validation
5. If still fails → spawn repair agent (attempt 3) with history
6. Re-run validation
7. If STILL fails → exhaustion:
   - File bead with full context
   - Unlock queue
   - Mark task as "merged_needs_repair"

## Exhaustion Bead Content

```markdown
## Validation Failure - Repair Exhausted

Task: {task_id} - {task_title}

### Validation Step
- Step: {step_name}
- Command: {command}
- Final output: {output}

### Repair Attempts
1. Attempt 1: {summary}
2. Attempt 2: {summary}
3. Attempt 3: {summary}

### Merged Diff
{diff}

### Action Required
Manual intervention needed to fix validation.
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] max_repair_attempts configurable
- [ ] Retry loop with attempt tracking
- [ ] Previous attempts passed to next repair agent
- [ ] Exhaustion files bead with full context
- [ ] Queue unlocks after exhaustion
- [ ] Task marked with appropriate status

title: Merge queue leaks .canopy/ resolver artifacts into commits
description:
## Problem

The merge queue doesn't filter out `.canopy/` directory files during merge. When a resolver agent runs, it writes context files to `.canopy/conflict/` in its overlay. These files get merged into the main repo and committed.

## Root Cause

In `pkg/merge/sequential.go`:
- `isBeadsFile()` filters `.beads/` directory (line 178-181)
- No equivalent filter for `.canopy/`
- Resolver writes to `.canopy/conflict/` (pkg/resolver/resolver.go:222)
- These files are applied via `applyChange()` and staged

## Evidence

Commit cdb2e59 incorrectly included:
```
.canopy/conflict/errors.txt
.canopy/conflict/original-task.txt
.canopy/conflict/patch-0.patch
```

## Solution

Add `isCanopyFile()` filter similar to `isBeadsFile()`:

```go
func isCanopyFile(path string) bool {
    return path == ".canopy" || strings.HasPrefix(path, ".canopy/")
}
```

Apply in the same places as isBeadsFile (lines 107, 159, 321).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.canopy/` files are never merged from overlays
- [ ] `.canopy/` files are never staged or committed
- [ ] Resolver conflict context still works (files remain in overlay only)

title: Create active_overlays table for tracking
description:
## Summary

Create database table to track active overlay filesystems, enabling recovery after daemon restart.

## Background

Overlays are the sandbox filesystem where agents work. Currently:
- Created in-memory by scheduler
- Cleaned up when process exits
- Lost on crash/restart

For agent resumability, we need to persist overlay metadata so we can remount them after daemon restart.

## Implementation

### 1. Migration V14 (`pkg/persistence/migrate.go`)

```go
func (s *Store) migrateV14(tx *sql.Tx) error {
    schema := `
        CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS active_overlays (
            agent_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
            task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
            session_id TEXT,
            upper_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
            merged_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
            lower_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
            work_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
            created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
            status TEXT DEFAULT 'active',
            FOREIGN KEY (agent_id) REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
        );
        
        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_active_overlays_status ON active_overlays(status);
        CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_active_overlays_run_id ON active_overlays(run_id);
    `
    _, err := tx.Exec(schema)
    return err
}
```

### 2. Add persistence methods (`pkg/persistence/store.go`)

```go
type ActiveOverlay struct {
    AgentID   string `json:"agent_id"`
    TaskID    string `json:"task_id"`
    RunID     string `json:"run_id"`
    SessionID string `json:"session_id,omitempty"`
    UpperDir  string `json:"upper_dir"`
    MergedDir string `json:"merged_dir"`
    LowerDir  string `json:"lower_dir"`
    WorkDir   string `json:"work_dir"`
    CreatedAt int64  `json:"created_at"`
    Status    string `json:"status"` // active, completed, orphaned
}

func (s *Store) TrackOverlay(overlay *ActiveOverlay) error
func (s *Store) UpdateOverlaySessionID(agentID, sessionID string) error
func (s *Store) MarkOverlayCompleted(agentID string) error
func (s *Store) GetActiveOverlays() ([]*ActiveOverlay, error)
func (s *Store) GetOrphanedOverlays() ([]*ActiveOverlay, error)
func (s *Store) DeleteOverlay(agentID string) error
```

### 3. Integrate with scheduler

When scheduler creates overlay:
```go
// After overlay.Mount()
d.persistence.TrackOverlay(&persistence.ActiveOverlay{
    AgentID:   agentID,
    TaskID:    task.ID,
    RunID:     runID,
    UpperDir:  overlay.UpperDir,
    MergedDir: overlay.MergedDir,
    LowerDir:  overlay.LowerDir,
    WorkDir:   overlay.WorkDir,
    CreatedAt: time.Now().Unix(),
    Status:    "active",
})
```

When agent completes (success or failure):
```go
d.persistence.MarkOverlayCompleted(agentID)
// Then cleanup overlay filesystem
```

### 4. Update session_id when available

Session ID comes from Claude result (emitted partway through or at end):
```go
// When result event received with session_id
d.persistence.UpdateOverlaySessionID(agentID, sessionID)
```

## Key Files

- `pkg/persistence/migrate.go` - Add migration V14
- `pkg/persistence/store.go` - Add ActiveOverlay type and methods
- `pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go` - Call TrackOverlay on mount
- `pkg/daemon/daemon.go` - Integrate overlay tracking

## Testing

- Unit test: CRUD operations for active_overlays
- Integration test: Overlay tracked on agent start, removed on complete
- Edge case: Agent crash leaves overlay in "active" status

## Dependencies

- Persist session_id in agents table (V13 migration first)

title: Add bidirectional control to IPC/API protocol
description:
## Summary

Enable control messages from CLI/UI to daemon for run management. Currently IPC is one-way (orchestrator → daemon events).

## Current State

- IPC: One-way, orchestrator sends events to daemon
- HTTP: REST API for queries and some control (pause/resume)
- WebSocket: One-way push from daemon to UI

## Analysis: IPC vs REST

For run control, we have two options:

### Option A: Extend IPC (Bidirectional)

Pros:
- Single communication channel
- Already connected during `canopy run`
- Lower latency

Cons:
- IPC designed for fire-and-forget events
- Would need request/response semantics
- More complex protocol changes

### Option B: Use REST API (Recommended)

Pros:
- REST already supports request/response
- Existing endpoints for pause/resume
- CLI can use same API as UI
- Simpler implementation

Cons:
- Two communication channels (IPC for events, REST for control)
- HTTP overhead (minimal)

## Recommendation

Use REST API for all control operations. This is simpler and consistent with existing pause/resume.

## Implementation

1. CLI uses REST for control:
   - `canopy run --stop` → `POST /api/runs/:id/stop`
   - `canopy run --status` → `GET /api/runs/active`
   - Start run → `POST /api/runs/start`

2. Keep IPC for high-volume events:
   - Agent output streaming
   - Live feed events
   - Status updates

3. WebSocket remains push-only:
   - UI receives events
   - UI uses REST for control actions

## New REST Endpoints

```
POST /api/runs/start
POST /api/runs/:id/stop
GET  /api/runs/active
GET  /api/runs/:id/status
PATCH /api/runs/:id/config
```

## Alternative: WebSocket Bidirectional

If we later want real-time control without REST:
- Add message types to WebSocket protocol
- Handle control messages in Hub
- More complex but lower latency

Not needed initially - REST is sufficient.

## Dependencies

- Move orchestrator lifecycle into daemon (API targets must exist)

title: Consolidate config files into single config.toml
description:
## Summary

Merge all `.canopy/*.toml` files into a single `.canopy/config.toml` with clear sections.

## Current State (Fragmented)

```
.canopy/
├── config.toml      # Just [resolver] timeout
├── sandbox.toml     # [sandbox], [resources], [paths], [security]
└── validation.toml  # [validation] steps
```

This is confusing - unclear where settings should go, and `config.toml` is nearly empty.

## Target State (Consolidated)

```toml
# .canopy/config.toml - Single configuration file

[resolver]
timeout = "10m"

[sandbox]
enabled = true
network = "allow"

[resources]
max_memory = "4GB"
max_processes = 100
max_open_files = 1024
timeout = "10m"

[paths]
read_only = ["~/.cargo", "~/.rustup"]
copy_configs = ["~/.gitconfig"]
cache_mounts = ["~/.cache/go-build", "~/go/pkg/mod"]

[paths.extra]
read_only = []
copy_configs = []

[security]
blocked = []

[validation]
enabled = true
mode = "strict"

[[validation.steps]]
name = "build"
command = "go build ./..."
required = true

[[validation.steps]]
name = "test"
command = "go test ./..."
required = false

[rules]
# Task selection rules (see rules epic)
priority_min = 0
priority_max = 4
# ... (defined in separate task)
```

## Implementation

### 1. Update config.go to load all sections

```go
type Config struct {
    Resolver   ResolverSettings   `toml:"resolver"`
    Sandbox    SandboxSettings    `toml:"sandbox"`
    Resources  ResourceSettings   `toml:"resources"`
    Paths      PathSettings       `toml:"paths"`
    Security   SecuritySettings   `toml:"security"`
    Validation ValidationSettings `toml:"validation"`
    Rules      RulesSettings      `toml:"rules"`
}
```

### 2. Migrate types from sandbox/config.go and validation/config.go

Move structs into `pkg/config/config.go` or create `pkg/config/types.go`.

### 3. Backward compatibility

Support loading old separate files during transition:
```go
func LoadConfig(workDir string) (*Config, error) {
    config := DefaultConfig()
    
    // Try consolidated config first
    if exists(".canopy/config.toml") {
        load and return
    }
    
    // Fall back to separate files (deprecated)
    if exists(".canopy/sandbox.toml") {
        warn("sandbox.toml is deprecated, merge into config.toml")
        loadSandboxInto(config)
    }
    // ... same for validation.toml
    
    return config
}
```

### 4. Update all callers

- `pkg/sandbox/*.go` - Use config.Sandbox instead of separate load
- `pkg/validation/*.go` - Use config.Validation instead of separate load
- `cmd/canopy/run.go` - Single config load

### 5. Update `canopy init`

Generate single `config.toml` instead of multiple files.

## Migration Path

1. Add support for consolidated config (new sections in Config struct)
2. Keep backward compat for separate files with deprecation warning
3. Update `canopy init` to generate consolidated config
4. Document migration in release notes
5. Remove separate file support in future version

## Key Files

- `pkg/config/config.go` - Expand Config struct
- `pkg/sandbox/config.go` - Deprecate, move types to config package
- `pkg/validation/config.go` - Deprecate, move types to config package
- `cmd/canopy/init.go` - Generate consolidated config

## Testing

- Load consolidated config
- Load legacy separate files with warning
- Validation of all sections

Reconstruct child_agent_ids on state restoration
description:
## Problem

The child_agent_ids array is shown in the Detail pane but is lost after daemon restart. Child agents (resolvers, repair agents) are not linked to their parents.

## Current State
- `parent_agent_id` IS persisted in SQLite (migration V7)
- `child_agent_ids` is computed at runtime when child agents start
- After restart, parent-child relationships exist in DB but not in memory

## Solution
On state restoration, after loading all agents:
1. Build a map of parent_agent_id → []child_agent_id
2. For each agent with children, populate its ChildAgentIDs slice

This is a simple post-processing step during `ApplyRestoredState()`.

## Implementation
```go
// In ApplyRestoredState, after loading agents:
childrenMap := make(map[string][]string)
for _, agent := range agents {
    if agent.ParentAgentID != "" {
        childrenMap[agent.ParentAgentID] = append(
            childrenMap[agent.ParentAgentID], 
            agent.ID,
        )
    }
}
for parentID, childIDs := range childrenMap {
    if parent, ok := state.Agents[parentID]; ok {
        parent.ChildAgentIDs = childIDs
    }
}
```

## Files to Modify
- pkg/daemon/state.go (ApplyRestoredState or ConvertPersistenceAgentToState)

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Child agent IDs shown in Detail pane after daemon restart
- [ ] Parent-child navigation works after restart

title: Persistence: Daemon EventBus integration
description:
Subscribe to daemon EventBus and persist all events to SQLite.

## File
- pkg/daemon/persistence_handler.go

## Implementation
```go
type PersistenceHandler struct {
    store    *persistence.Store
    eventBus *EventBus
}

func (h *PersistenceHandler) Start() func() {
    return h.eventBus.Subscribe(func(event Event) {
        switch event.Type {
        case EventRunStarted:
            h.store.CreateRun(...)
        case EventAgentStarted:
            h.store.CreateAgent(...)
        case EventAgentCompleted:
            h.store.UpdateAgent(...)
        case EventRunCompleted:
            h.store.UpdateRun(...)
        }
    })
}
```

## Integration
- Initialize in daemon.NewDaemon() if EnablePersistence config is true
- Close store in daemon.Stop()
- Handle errors gracefully (log, don't crash)

description:
## Problem

When merging file changes, applyChange() fails with:
```
open /tmp/canopy/.../upper/.claude.json.lock: permission denied
```

## Analysis

The merger reads files from `result.Overlay.UpperPath(change.Path)` and copies them to the host repo. This fails when:

1. Overlay is unmounted before merge completes
2. File permissions in overlay are restrictive
3. Race condition between agent completion and merge processing

title: Merge queue must filter gitignored files before staging
description:
## Problem

The merge queue tried to `git add` files that are in .gitignore, causing the commit to fail:

```
git add failed: exit status 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:
web/dashboard/dist
web/dashboard/src/App.d.ts
web/dashboard/src/App.js
...
```

## Root Cause

Three-part failure in the merge pipeline:

### 1. Overlay captures everything (pkg/sandbox/overlay.go:349)
`GetChanges()` detects all filesystem changes in the sandbox but has no gitignore awareness - it just reports what's physically in the overlay.

### 2. Merge filtering is incomplete (pkg/merge/sequential.go:350-365)
Current filters:
- .beads/ files ✓
- .canopy/ files ✓  
- Overlay whiteout markers ✓
- Transient files (locks, backups) ✓
- **Gitignored files ✗ MISSING**

### 3. Git add with explicit paths bypasses gitignore
```go
addCmd := exec.Command("git", "add", "--")
addCmd.Args = append(addCmd.Args, paths...)  // Explicit paths bypass .gitignore
```

When you run `git add -- file1 file2`, Git adds the files even if they're in .gitignore because they're explicitly named.

## Solution

Add a gitignore filter before staging. Options:

### Option A: Use `git check-ignore` to filter paths
```go
// Before staging, filter out gitignored files
var filteredPaths []string
for _, path := range paths {
    cmd := exec.Command("git", "check-ignore", "-q", path)
    if cmd.Run() != nil { // exit 1 = not ignored
        filteredPaths = append(filteredPaths, path)
    }
}
```

### Option B: Use `git add` without explicit paths
Stage all changes and let git respect .gitignore:
```go
addCmd := exec.Command("git", "add", ".")  // Respects .gitignore
```

### Option C: Parse .gitignore and filter in Go
Use a library like `go-gitignore` to filter paths before staging.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Gitignored files are never staged by merge queue
- [ ] Resolver also respects gitignore (uses same pipeline)
- [ ] Test with web/dashboard TypeScript compilation artifacts

title: IPC protocol version negotiation not actually used
description:
## Problem

The IPC protocol defines v1 (legacy) and v2 (current) with version fields, but:
- Server accepts both but treats them identically
- Client always sends v2
- No actual protocol negotiation happens
- Size limits only apply to v2 but check happens after parsing

Location: pkg/ipc/protocol.go:86-163

## Impact

- Over-engineered for no current benefit
- False sense of backwards compatibility
- Size limit protection is ineffective (DoS can still occur)

## Suggested Fix

1. Remove v1 support if no legacy clients exist
2. Move size checking to before JSON parsing (read raw bytes first)
3. Document actual compatibility requirements

title: Persistent daemon mode
description:
## Architecture Decision

The daemon will own and coordinate all orchestration with **true agent resumability** via `claude --resume`.

### Key Requirements

1. **Daemon owns orchestration**: `canopy run` delegates the entire run to the daemon
2. **Singleton enforcement**: Only one active canopy run per repository checkout
3. **Indefinite mode**: Runs can be "execute beads as they come up" instead of "execute until done"
4. **UI control**: Dashboard can start/stop/configure runs for any repo the daemon knows about
5. **Agent resumability**: Daemon restart does NOT lose in-flight work - agents resume via `claude --resume`

### Key Insight: `claude --resume`

Claude CLI supports `--resume <session-id>` which continues an existing conversation. Combined with overlay persistence, this gives us true agent resumability:

- **Session ID**: Captured from Claude output, persisted to SQLite
- **Overlay**: Upper/merged dirs tracked in `active_overlays` table
- **On daemon restart**: Remount overlay + `claude --resume <session-id>`
- **Agent continues**: Same conversation context, sees its partial work

### Target Architecture

```
canopy run (thin client)
  └─> Tells daemon to start run
  └─> Streams output
  └─> Can disconnect (run continues)

Daemon (background)
  └─> Owns Orchestrator per repo
      └─> Runs agents (tracks session_id + overlay)
      └─> Manages merge queue
      └─> Watch mode: polls for new tasks
  └─> On restart:
      └─> Queries active_overlays table
      └─> Remounts overlays
      └─> Resumes agents with claude --resume
  └─> Enforces singleton runs per repo
  └─> Serves UI with full run control
```

### Database Schema Additions

```sql
-- Add to agents table
ALTER TABLE agents ADD COLUMN session_id TEXT;

-- New table for tracking active overlays
CREATE TABLE active_overlays (
    agent_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    session_id TEXT,
    upper_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
    merged_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
    work_dir TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    FOREIGN KEY (agent_id) REFERENCES agents(id)
);
```

### Implementation Sequence

1. Persist session_id in agents table (migration V13)
2. Create active_overlays table for tracking (migration V14)
3. Move orchestrator lifecycle into daemon
4. Implement overlay recovery on daemon restart
5. Implement agent resume with `claude --resume`
6. CLI delegation (thin client)
7. Run singleton enforcement
8. Indefinite/watch mode
9. UI run controls

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Session ID persisted for every agent
- [ ] Active overlays tracked in database
- [ ] Daemon restart recovers in-flight agents
- [ ] Agents resume with full conversation context
- [ ] `canopy run` is a thin client that delegates to daemon
- [ ] Daemon rejects concurrent runs for same repo
- [ ] `canopy run --watch` runs indefinitely
- [ ] Dashboard has Start Run / Stop Run buttons
- [ ] Run continues if `canopy run` CLI disconnects

title: Plugin agents: Extensible agent system with trigger rules and composition
description:
## Problem

Canopy has three hard-coded agent types (implementor, resolver, repair) with no extension mechanism. Users cannot:

1. Add custom agent types (linter, formatter, security scanner)
2. Define trigger rules (run on every commit, on file patterns)
3. Compose agents (chain outputs, parallel fan-out)
4. Choose sync vs async execution per agent type

## Solution

Create a plugin agent system with:
- Agent type registry with interface contract
- Declarative trigger rules in config
- Composition primitives (chain, fan-out, gate)
- Sync/async execution modes

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Plugin format**: Go interface + config, not external binaries (initially)
2. **Trigger rules**: File patterns, commit count, manual, post-merge
3. **Composition**: DAG-based with dependency tracking
4. **Sync mode**: Block merge queue vs run in parallel
5. **Configuration**: .canopy/agents.toml for custom agents

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Custom agent types can be registered
- [ ] Trigger rules execute agents automatically
- [ ] Agent chains work with output passing
- [ ] Sync agents block merge queue
- [ ] Async agents run concurrently

## Problem

```go
CurrentRunID string `json:"current_run_id"`
```

1. Set when `run_started` is received (state.go:838)

title: Resolver agents missing parent_agent_id after migration V8
description:
## Problem

Merge resolver agents appear as separate cards in the dashboard instead of being grouped under their parent agent.

## Root Cause

The migration V8 backfill for `parent_agent_id` ran once, but resolver agents created between that migration and the code fix (commit 391534f) were never backfilled. These orphaned resolvers show as standalone cards.

## Evidence

Query found 10 resolver agents with missing `parent_agent_id` that should have matched:
```sql
SELECT id, parent_agent_id FROM agents 
WHERE id LIKE '%-resolver' 
  AND (parent_agent_id IS NULL OR parent_agent_id = '');
```

Manual backfill fixed them:
```sql
UPDATE agents SET parent_agent_id = (
    SELECT parent.id FROM agents parent 
    WHERE parent.run_id = agents.run_id 
      AND parent.task_id = agents.task_id 
      AND parent.id != agents.id 
      AND parent.id NOT LIKE '%-resolver' 
    LIMIT 1
) WHERE agents.id LIKE '%-resolver' 
  AND (parent_agent_id IS NULL OR parent_agent_id = '');
```

## Solution

Add a startup backfill routine in the persistence layer that runs the same query on daemon startup. This ensures any orphaned resolvers get their `parent_agent_id` populated regardless of when they were created.

Alternatively, add migration V10 (or next available) that re-runs the backfill.
close_reason: Resolved: Historical orphaned resolver agents were manually backfilled. The main issue (canopy-si3m) was stale JS files in dashboard src.

Daemon: Persist state to XDG_CACHE_HOME with SQLite
description:
Persist daemon state to $XDG_CACHE_HOME/canopy/runs.db using SQLite (WAL mode).

## Recommendation: SQLite
- ACID transactions for crash recovery
- Fast queries for historical data ("show runs from last week")
- Single file, pure Go driver (modernc.org/sqlite)
- Perfect for expected volume (dozens to hundreds of runs/day)

## Directory Structure
```
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/canopy/
├── runs.db           # Main SQLite database
├── runs.db-wal       # Write-ahead log
└── logs/             # Optional full agent logs
```

## Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE runs (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    finished_at INTEGER,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,  -- running, completed, cancelled, failed
    concurrency INTEGER NOT NULL,
    git_branch TEXT,
    git_commit TEXT,
    total_tasks INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    completed_tasks INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    failed_tasks INTEGER DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE TABLE agents (
    id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    task_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    task_title TEXT NOT NULL,
    status TEXT NOT NULL,
    started_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    finished_at INTEGER,
    duration_seconds REAL,
    exit_code INTEGER,
    error_message TEXT,
    stdout TEXT,
    stderr TEXT,
    input_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    output_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    total_tokens INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    cost_usd REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
    files_changed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    git_commits_created INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    FOREIGN KEY (run_id) REFERENCES runs(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE git_commits (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    commit_sha TEXT NOT NULL,
    author_name TEXT,
    author_email TEXT,
    commit_message TEXT,
    timestamp INTEGER NOT NULL,
    files_changed INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    FOREIGN KEY (agent_id) REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE file_changes (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    agent_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    run_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    file_path TEXT NOT NULL,
    change_type TEXT NOT NULL,  -- created, modified, deleted
    size_bytes INTEGER,
    FOREIGN KEY (agent_id) REFERENCES agents(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
```

## Implementation
- pkg/persistence/store.go - Store struct with CRUD operations
- pkg/persistence/migrate.go - Schema versioning and migrations
- pkg/daemon/persistence_handler.go - EventBus subscriber for persistence

## Key Features
- WAL mode for concurrent reads/writes
- Connection pool: 5 max open, 2 idle
- Automatic schema migrations
- Query helpers: ListRuns(filter), GetStats(since), GetAgentsByRun(id)

title: Dashboard run selector doesn't show current run
description:
## Problem

When a new canopy run starts, the "All runs" dropdown shows historical runs but NOT the currently active run. Users cannot filter to see just the current run's agents.

## Root Cause

1. Dashboard loads runs from DB via `getRuns()` on page load (Dashboard.tsx:177)
2. WebSocket `agent:started` events include `run_id` but don't trigger run creation
3. The store has `addRun` and `updateRun` methods (stateStore.ts:437-453) that are **never called**

## Solution Options

**Option A (Preferred):** Backend sends `run:started` event
- Add `run:started` event to IPC protocol
- Daemon publishes event when `canopy run` creates a new run
- Dashboard calls `addRun` on receiving the event

**Option B:** Frontend infers new runs
- In `agent:started` handler, check if `run_id` exists in `runs` array
- If not, create a placeholder Run and call `addRun`
- Update run stats as agents complete

## Files to Modify

- pkg/ipc/protocol.go - Add RunStarted event type
- pkg/ipc/server.go - Publish run:started on run creation  
- web/dashboard/src/hooks/useWebSocket.ts - Handle run:started event
- web/dashboard/src/stores/stateStore.ts - Run update logic already exists

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New canopy run appears in dropdown immediately when started
- [ ] Run shows as "Running" with pulsing indicator
- [ ] Selecting the run filters to just its agents
- [ ] Run status updates to completed/failed when done

title: Persist merge results in database
description:
## Problem

Merge results from the merge queue are not persisted to the database. There's no record of:
- Which tasks were merged successfully
- Which tasks had merge conflicts
- Whether resolver was spawned
- Commit hashes created

## Current State

The persistence layer (pkg/persistence) tracks runs and agents but has no merge-related tables or fields.

## Solution

Add merge tracking to persistence:
1. Add merge_results table or merge fields to agents table
2. Track: merge_status, commits_applied, had_conflict, resolver_spawned
3. Update persistence handler to capture merge events

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Merge status persisted per agent
- [ ] Commits applied count recorded
- [ ] Conflict/resolver status tracked
- [ ] History viewable in dashboard

title: Dashboard: Show resolver agents as card extension, not separate cards
description:
## Problem

When a merge conflict occurs, the resolver agent appears as its own separate card. This clutters the UI and makes it unclear which resolver belongs to which task.

## Solution

Display resolver agents as a visual extension of their parent agent card:

- Resolver card slides out from behind the parent card (like a playing card)
- Offset slightly to show it's a child/extension
- Visual connection between parent and resolver
- Collapse/expand to show resolver details

## Visual Design

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│ Parent Agent Card   │
│ canopy-xyz1         │
│ Status: resolving   │
└─────────────────────┘
   ┌─────────────────────┐  ← Resolver card offset/behind
   │ Resolver            │
   │ Fixing conflicts... │
   └─────────────────────┘
```

## Implementation

- Track parent_agent_id relationship (already exists in agent results)
- Group resolver cards with their parent in UI
- CSS for stacked card effect
- Click to expand/focus resolver

## Files to Change

- `web/dashboard/src/components/AgentCard.tsx`
- `web/dashboard/src/components/AgentGrid.tsx` (or similar)

1. **Status-colored background**: Resolver card background should match status:
   - Amber/yellow for actively resolving
   - Red for failed resolution  
   - Green for successful resolution

3. **Compact height**: Smaller than regular cards since it's supplementary info

4. **Position**: At the BOTTOM of parent card, not offset to the side

title: Implement repair exhaustion: file bead and unlock queue
description:
When max attempts reached, file a bead and unlock the queue.

## Changes
- Detect exhaustion (attempts >= max_repair_attempts)
- Create bead with full context (validation output, repair summaries, diff)
- Call queue unlock to unblock other tasks
- Mark task status as 'merged_needs_repair'

## Bead Content
```markdown
## Validation Failure - Repair Exhausted

Task: {task_id} - {task_title}

### Validation Step
- Step: {step_name}
- Command: {command}
- Final output: {output}

### Repair Attempts
1. Attempt 1: {summary}
2. Attempt 2: {summary}
3. Attempt 3: {summary}

### Merged Diff
{diff}

### Action Required
Manual intervention needed to fix validation.
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bead filed with full context on exhaustion
- [ ] Queue unlocked after exhaustion
- [ ] Task marked 'merged_needs_repair'

title: Make agent timeout configurable
description:
## Location
`pkg/agent/executor.go:20`

## Problem
- Hardcoded 10-minute timeout for all tasks
- Short tasks waste time on long timeout
- Long tasks arbitrarily killed
- No per-task override capability

## Solution
1. Add Timeout field to agent config
2. Default to 10 minutes for backwards compatibility
3. Allow override in sandbox config
4. Consider per-task timeout in beads metadata

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Configurable default timeout
- [ ] Per-task override option
- [ ] Documentation updated

title: Consolidate IPC and daemon state types
description: Types like MergeStatus, AgentResult are duplicated between pkg/ipc/protocol.go and pkg/daemon/state.go. Create a shared types package or move the canonical definitions to one location with imports from the other. This reduces conversion overhead and prevents drift.

title: Dashboard doesn't show pending beads when no active repository is set
description:
## Problem

When the daemon starts with no active repository set, pending beads don't show in the UI.

## Root Cause Chain

1. No runs persisted (due to IPC event mapping bug - see related P0 bead)
2. restoreStateFromDB() finds no runs
3. No active repository is set
4. loadTasksFromBeads() can't get beads client (no active repo)
5. No tasks loaded
6. BeadsPane shows empty

## After P0 fix

Once runs are persisted correctly:
1. restoreStateFromDB() will find most recent run
2. Active repo will be set from run context
3. loadTasksFromBeads() will work
4. BeadsPane will show pending tasks

## Verification

After fixing the P0 IPC bug:
1. Run canopy at least once
2. Restart daemon
3. Verify /api/state shows tasks
4. Verify BeadsPane displays them

## Files
- pkg/daemon/daemon.go (loadTasksFromBeads, restoreStateFromDB)

title: Design repair agent prompt and context builder
description:
## Summary

Design the prompt template and context builder for repair agents.

## Prompt Requirements

The repair agent needs to understand:
1. **What failed**: Validation step name, command, output
2. **What was merged**: The diff that triggered validation
3. **What to do**: Fix the issue without breaking other things
4. **Constraints**: Don't revert the merge, don't break other tests

## Prompt Structure

```
You are a repair agent. A validation check failed after a merge.

## What Failed
Step: {step_name}
Command: {command}
Exit code: {exit_code}
Output:
{stdout}
{stderr}

## What Was Merged
{merged_diff}

## Previous Repair Attempts (if any)
{previous_attempts}

## Your Task
Fix the validation failure. Do NOT:
- Revert the merged changes
- Break other tests/functionality
- Make unrelated changes

Commit your fix with message: "fix: repair validation failure in {step_name}"
```

## Implementation

### File: `pkg/repairagent/prompt.go`
- BuildRepairPrompt(ctx *RepairContext) string
- Truncate large outputs to fit context window
- Include relevant file snippets from diff

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Prompt template designed and reviewed
- [ ] Context builder handles large outputs (truncation)
- [ ] Previous attempts included in context
- [ ] Clear instructions for agent behavior

Add macOS support using APFS copy-on-write clones instead of overlayFS. APFS clones are instant (metadata-only operation) and provide similar copy-on-write semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Change detection via mtime snapshots
- [ ] Proper cleanup of clone directories
- [ ] Clear error message for non-APFS filesystems

title: Beads task IDs not visible in daemon history UI

- agents.task_id column stores bead IDs
- EventAgentStarted captures task_id at creation time
- State restoration loads agents but may not properly display bead linkage

## Expected Behavior
Historical runs should show bead IDs and link back to the beads pane for context.

CRITICAL: Merge queue silent cleanup failure allows processing to continue with dirty state
description:
## Problem

When `resetToHead()` fails during merge cleanup, the failure is silently logged (only in verbose mode) and processing continues. This allows the merge queue to proceed with a dirty working directory.

## Location

`pkg/merge/sequential.go` lines 391-399:

```go
if err != nil {
    // Commit failed - reset working directory to clean HEAD state
    if resetErr := m.resetToHead(headCommit, paths); resetErr != nil && m.verbose {
        fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "warning: failed to reset working directory after merge failure: %v\n", resetErr)
    }
    mergeResult.Errors = append(mergeResult.Errors,
        fmt.Sprintf("failed to commit changes from %s: %v", result.TaskID, err))
}
// Processing continues regardless of resetErr!
```

## Problem

1. `resetErr` is only logged if `m.verbose` is true
2. Even if logged, processing continues
3. Working directory may be dirty but merge queue keeps going
4. No verification that cleanup actually succeeded

## Fix Required

1. Make cleanup failure a hard error, not a warning
2. Add post-cleanup verification that working directory is clean
3. If cleanup fails, either:
   - Force `git reset --hard HEAD` as fallback
   - Abort the entire merge run with clear error message

## Invariant

After ANY merge operation (success or failure), the working directory MUST be in a clean state (no uncommitted changes).

title: Resolver loops infinitely on stale overlay with permission denied
description:
## Problem

When a resolver completes and its overlay becomes inaccessible (permission denied or deleted), subsequent merge attempts keep referencing the stale resolver and fail in a loop.

## Observed Behavior

canopy-mxbf kept restarting because:
1. Worker agent completed and produced changes
2. Merge conflict detected, resolver spawned (`agent-435263fc-canopy-mxbf-resolver`)
3. Resolver completed, changes stored in overlay
4. Main merge tried to apply resolver changes but overlay inaccessible:
   ```
   resolver merge error for canopy-mxbf: failed to apply pkg/orchestrator/prompt.go from agent-435263fc-canopy-mxbf-resolver: open /home/john/.cache/canopy/overlays/.../upper/pkg/orchestrator/prompt.go: permission denied
   ```
5. Task marked as needing retry, worker agent restarts
6. Same resolver ID referenced, same permission error
7. Loop continues indefinitely

The task restarted 11+ times with identical resolver merge errors (see canopy-mxbf comments).

## Root Cause

The merge processor caches resolver results by agent ID and keeps trying to apply from the same overlay even when:
- The overlay has been cleaned up
- Files in the overlay have permission issues
- The overlay directory doesn't exist

## Expected Behavior

1. If resolver overlay is inaccessible, spawn a NEW resolver (don't reuse stale one)
2. Or: detect permission errors and fail fast with actionable error
3. Or: implement overlay recovery before attempting to read

## Files to Investigate

- `pkg/mergequeue/processor.go` - resolver result caching/reuse logic
- `pkg/overlay/manager.go` - overlay lifecycle management
- `pkg/orchestrator/orchestrator.go` - retry/restart logic

## Workaround

Manually complete the task and close the bead. Clean up stale overlays with `rm -rf ~/.cache/canopy/overlays/*`.

title: CRITICAL: Pre-commit hook failure should spawn repair agent with 3-way merge context
description:
## Problem

When git commit fails due to pre-commit hook rejection (e.g., build failure), the merge queue attempts cleanup but leaves uncommitted changes. Instead, it should spawn a repair agent with the 3-way merge context so the agent can fix the issue.

## Current Behavior

1. Agent completes work in overlay
2. Merge queue applies changes to working directory
3. `git commit` runs, pre-commit hook fails (build error)
4. Merge queue tries `git reset HEAD` (only unstages)
5. Working directory left dirty - changes orphaned

## Expected Behavior

1. Agent completes work in overlay
2. Merge queue applies changes to working directory
3. `git commit` runs, pre-commit hook fails
4. **Spawn repair agent** with:
   - The 3-way merge diff (base, ours, theirs)
   - Pre-commit hook error output
   - Task context (which bead, what was being implemented)
5. Repair agent fixes the issue and commits
6. If repair fails after max attempts, THEN revert and file issue

## Location

`pkg/merge/sequential.go` - `commitFileChanges()` and `MergeSingle()`

The validation/repair flow already exists for post-merge validation. Pre-commit hook failures should use the same repair mechanism.

## Key Insight

Pre-commit hook failure IS a validation failure - it's just happening at commit time instead of post-merge. The repair agent infrastructure should handle both cases.

## Evidence

From logs:
```
git commit failed: exit status 1
pkg/daemon/recovery.go:93:21: undefined: sandbox.UnmountPath
```

A repair agent could easily fix this by adding the missing function or import.

title: Persist parent_agent_id to database for resolver card grouping
description:
## Problem

Resolver agents show as standalone cards when viewing history or after daemon restart, instead of being grouped with their parent agent as stacked sub-cards.

## Root Cause

`parent_agent_id` is tracked in runtime state but NOT persisted to the database:

- `pkg/ipc/protocol.go` - IPC events include `parent_agent_id`
- `pkg/daemon/state.go` - AgentState has `ParentAgentID` field
- `pkg/resolver/resolver.go` - Sets it when spawning resolvers

But:
- `pkg/persistence/store.go` - Agent struct has NO `parent_agent_id` column
- `pkg/persistence/migrate.go` - No migration for it

## Impact

- Live resolver agents: ✅ Show as stacked sub-cards (parent linkage in memory)
- Historical resolver agents: ❌ Show as standalone cards (linkage lost)
- After daemon restart: ❌ Linkage lost even for recent agents

## Solution

1. Add `parent_agent_id` column to agents table (migration)
2. Update `Agent` struct in store.go
3. Persist parent_agent_id in CreateAgent/UpdateAgent
4. Load parent_agent_id in GetAgent/GetAgentsByRun
5. Restore linkage in daemon's `restoreStateFromDB()`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Historical resolver agents grouped with parent in UI
- [ ] Daemon restart preserves parent-child linkage
- [ ] Migration handles existing agents (NULL parent_agent_id OK)

title: Enforce singleton canopy runs per repository
description:
## Summary

Ensure only one canopy run can be active per repository checkout. The daemon enforces this constraint.

## Current State

- No enforcement of singleton runs
- Multiple `canopy run` processes could theoretically run simultaneously
- This would cause merge conflicts, race conditions, beads corruption

## Target State

- Daemon tracks active run per repository (by absolute path)
- New run requests for same repo are rejected with clear error
- Optional: queue mode where new runs wait for current to complete

## Implementation

1. Add active run tracking to OrchestratorManager:
   ```go
   type OrchestratorManager struct {
       activeRuns map[string]*ActiveRun // keyed by repo path
       mu         sync.RWMutex
   }
   
   type ActiveRun struct {
       RunID       string
       RepoPath    string
       StartedAt   time.Time
       Orchestrator *orchestrator.Orchestrator
   }
   ```

2. Check before starting new run:
   ```go
   func (m *OrchestratorManager) StartRun(repoPath string, ...) error {
       m.mu.Lock()
       defer m.mu.Unlock()
       
       if existing, ok := m.activeRuns[repoPath]; ok {
           return fmt.Errorf("run already active for %s (run_id=%s, started=%s)",
               repoPath, existing.RunID, existing.StartedAt)
       }
       // ... create and start
   }
   ```

3. Clean up on run completion:
   - Remove from activeRuns map when orchestrator completes
   - Handle both success and failure cases

4. Expose via API for UI visibility:
   - `GET /api/runs/active` - list active runs by repo
   - Include run parameters and duration

## Error Message

When rejecting concurrent run:
```
Error: A canopy run is already active for this repository.

  Run ID:    canopy-abc123
  Started:   2 minutes ago
  Repo:      /home/user/myproject

Use "canopy run --status" to check progress, or "canopy run --stop" to terminate.
```

## Dependencies

- Move orchestrator lifecycle into daemon (must complete first)

title: Resolver missing three-way merge context causes reverts
description:
## Problem

Merge resolvers are reverting legitimate changes from other agents. This happens because resolvers lack sufficient context to understand the three-way merge situation.

### Current State

When a conflict occurs, the resolver receives:
- Task metadata (ID, title, description)  
- The failed patches (git format-patch output)
- Error messages from `git am --3way`
- A fresh overlay based on current HEAD

### What's Missing

1. **Base commit hash** - The patches are diffs relative to a specific commit, but the resolver doesn't know which one

2. **Base-to-HEAD diff** - The resolver can't see what changed between the agent's starting point and current HEAD. This is crucial for understanding WHY the conflict occurred

3. **File content at base commit** - For conflicting files, the resolver needs to see original state

### Example Failure Scenario

1. Agent A starts at commit `abc123` where file has `foo(x, y)`
2. Agent A adds a parameter: `foo(x, y, z)`
3. Agent B concurrently adds `bar()` function below `foo()`, merges first
4. HEAD is now `def456` with `foo(x, y)` and `bar()`
5. Agent A's patch fails (context lines don't match due to missing `bar()`)
6. **Resolver sees HEAD** which has `bar()`, but patch doesn't mention it
7. Resolver thinks: "patch expects no `bar()`, must remove it"
8. **REVERT**: `bar()` gets removed

### Solution

Provide proper three-way merge context:

1. Add `BaseCommit` to ConflictContext (already in GitState, just not passed)
2. Generate `git diff <base>..<HEAD>` to show what changed concurrently  
3. For conflicting files specifically, include the file content at base commit
4. Update resolver prompt to explain the three-way relationship:
   - BASE: What code looked like when agent started
   - OURS: Current HEAD (what resolver sees)
   - THEIRS: What agent's patches intended to change
5. Resolver should preserve OURS changes and incorporate THEIRS intent

### Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Resolver receives base commit hash in ConflictContext
- [ ] Resolver receives diff showing concurrent changes (base..HEAD)
- [ ] Resolver prompt explains three-way merge semantics
- [ ] Resolver no longer reverts concurrent changes
- [ ] Add test case for concurrent modification scenario

title: Canopy agents revert existing fixes when merging from stale snapshots
description:
## Problem

Canopy agents work from snapshots taken at task start. If a fix is made to main 
while agents are running, agents' changes can overwrite that fix when merged.

This has happened repeatedly with the beads/client.go Fail() fix - agents 
keep reverting it because they're working from pre-fix snapshots.

## Impact

Critical fixes get silently reverted, breaking the system repeatedly.

## Root Cause

The merge queue uses last-writer-wins for file conflicts. When an agent modifies 
a file that was also fixed on main, the agent's stale version wins.

## Solution

This is related to canopy-xn6q (proper merge resolver). The merge agent needs to:
1. Detect when HEAD has changed since agent started
2. Do a proper 3-way merge or rebase
3. Preserve fixes made to main, not blindly overwrite

## Workaround

Add comments like "DO NOT REVERT" to critical fixes, but this is fragile.
close_reason: Addressed by canopy-xn6q: reset HEAD on failure, pass patches to resolver

title: Create new agent record per run instead of reusing agent IDs across runs
description:
## Problem

When a task is retried in a new run, the same agent ID is reused (e.g., `agent-canopy-xyz`). This causes issues:

1. **Cross-run resolver orphans**: Resolver agents spawned in a new run can't find their parent agent because the parent is in a different run_id. Found 4 such orphaned resolvers during s5nn migration.

2. **History confusion**: The same agent ID appearing in multiple runs makes it unclear which run's execution you're looking at.

3. **Upsert semantics**: Current code uses `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE` which overwrites previous run's agent data.

## Expected Behavior

Each run should create a fresh agent record with a unique ID, even for the same task. For example:
- Run 1: `agent-canopy-xyz-run1` or `agent-{runID}-canopy-xyz`
- Run 2: `agent-canopy-xyz-run2` or `agent-{runID}-canopy-xyz`

This would also naturally solve the resolver parent matching since both parent and resolver would be in the same run.

## Current Behavior

Agent ID is derived solely from task ID: `agent-{taskID}`

## Impact

- Resolver agents can become orphaned in cross-run scenarios
- Run history may show incorrect/overwritten agent data
- Parent-child relationships break across runs

title: Beads/tasks not displayed in web dashboard
description:
## Problem

Beads/tasks not displayed in web dashboard due to repository filtering mismatch.

## Root Cause

`/api/state` always filters tasks by active repository ID, but tasks may be loaded with a different (or empty) RepoID:

1. Tasks loaded at daemon startup get `RepoID = GetActiveRepositoryID()` (often empty)
2. When repository changes, old tasks keep their original RepoID
3. `GetSnapshotForRepo(activeRepoID)` filters out tasks where `task.RepoID != activeRepoID`
4. Frontend receives empty tasks array

**Key code path:**
- `pkg/daemon/handlers.go:87` - `GetSnapshotForRepo(activeRepoID)`
- `pkg/daemon/state.go:454-461` - Filtering: `if task.RepoID == repoID`
- `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:352` - Tasks loaded with potentially wrong RepoID

## Fix Options

**Option A: Don't filter tasks by repo (simplest)**
- Change `handlers.go:87` to use `GetSnapshot()` instead of `GetSnapshotForRepo()`
- Tasks from all repos shown (may need UI filtering instead)

**Option B: Reload tasks on repo switch**
- In `SetActiveRepository()`, clear ALL tasks and reload with correct RepoID
- Currently only clears tasks with empty RepoID

**Option C: Fix RepoID assignment**
- Ensure tasks always get correct RepoID when loaded
- Re-tag existing tasks when repo changes

## Files to Change

- `pkg/daemon/handlers.go:87` - State endpoint filtering
- `pkg/daemon/state.go:454-461` - GetSnapshotForRepo filtering
- `pkg/daemon/daemon.go:100-107` - SetActiveRepository task clearing

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tasks appear in dashboard when daemon starts
- [ ] Tasks remain visible after repository switch
- [ ] New tasks from canopy run appear in real-time
